items.followUp: What is the purpose of a router in a computer network?

rubric.why: Identifies that routing determines an appropriate path for data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that routing selects or determines the best route/path.

rubric.why: Identifies how routing helps data reach its destination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the selected route is used to forward packets towards the destination.

modelAnswer: Routing determines the best available path for data packets to travel from the source to the destination.
Routers use this path to forward the packets through the network.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a hub and a switch.

rubric.why: States what colspan controls in an HTML table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that colspan makes a cell span across multiple columns.

rubric.why: States what rowspan controls in an HTML table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that rowspan makes a cell span across multiple rows.

modelAnswer: The colspan attribute makes a table cell extend across two or more columns.
The rowspan attribute makes a table cell extend across two or more rows.

items.followUp: What is an ordered list in HTML, and which tags are used to create it?

rubric.why: Describes how items in an unordered list are displayed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an unordered list displays items with bullets or other markers, not a numbered sequence.

rubric.why: Identifies the HTML tag used to create the list.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the <ul> tag; accept mention of <li> as the item tag when paired with a correct unordered-list description.

modelAnswer: An unordered list displays related items with bullets or other markers, without a particular sequence.
It is created with the <ul> tag, and each item is written inside an <li> tag.

items.followUp: Explain the difference between a character and a string in text data.

rubric.why: Identifies one basic type of text data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a character is a single letter, digit, or symbol.

rubric.why: Describes what a character may contain.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving a correct example or description of a character.

rubric.why: Identifies the other basic type of text data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a string is a sequence of characters.

rubric.why: Clarifies how a string differs from a single character.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that a string can contain multiple characters, such as a word or sentence.

modelAnswer: Text data is commonly represented as character data and string data.
A character is a single letter, digit, or symbol, such as 'A' or '7'.
A string is a sequence of characters, such as a word, name, or sentence.
For example, 'A' is a character, while 'Ali' is a string.

items.followUp: Name and explain the sender, receiver, and transmission medium in a communication system.

rubric.why: Identifies the origin of the communication.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the sender as the device or person that sends the message.

rubric.why: Identifies the recipient of the communication.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the receiver as the device or person that receives the message.

rubric.why: Identifies the information being communicated.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the message as the information or data being sent.

rubric.why: Identifies a means or rule involved in transferring information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the transmission medium as the path/channel used to carry the message, or naming the protocol as the rules governing communication.

modelAnswer: The sender is the device or person that sends the message.
The receiver is the device or person that receives the message.
The message is the information or data being communicated.
The transmission medium is the path or channel through which the message travels; protocols are the rules used for communication.

items.followUp: Explain any four measures that help protect data from security threats.

rubric.why: Names a valid ethical concern relating to data security.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that personal or confidential data should be protected from unauthorized access or disclosure.

rubric.why: Names a valid ethical concern relating to data security.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that data should remain correct and should not be improperly changed.

rubric.why: Names a valid ethical concern relating to data and its ownership.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that data has an owner and must not be copied or used without permission.

rubric.why: Names a valid ethical concern relating to access to data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that access should be available to authorized users and restricted for unauthorized users.

modelAnswer: Privacy: Personal and confidential data should not be accessed or disclosed without permission.
Accuracy: Data should be correct and should not be changed improperly.
Property: Data has an owner, so it should not be copied or used without permission.
Accessibility: Authorized users should be able to access data, while unauthorized users should be prevented from doing so.

items.followUp: Which flowchart symbol is used to show input and output?

rubric.why: Identifies one use of the terminal symbol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the terminal symbol shows the start or beginning of a flowchart.

rubric.why: Identifies the other use of the terminal symbol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the terminal symbol shows the end or termination of a flowchart.

modelAnswer: The terminal symbol is used to show the start or beginning of a flowchart.
It is also used to show the end or termination of a flowchart.

items.followUp: How can a trace table help when testing an algorithm?

rubric.why: Identifies the information recorded in a trace table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a trace table records variable values during execution.

rubric.why: Explains how a trace table follows an algorithm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it tracks the algorithm step by step to check its operation or find errors.

modelAnswer: A trace table records the values of variables as an algorithm is executed.
It follows the algorithm step by step and helps check its operation or find errors.
